latestRelease.notes:
## This is a patch release.

### What's Changed

- Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following `AUTH`, `SELECT`, `HELLO`, `CLIENT`, or `RESET` now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state ([#8016](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8016)).
- Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation ([#8011](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8011), [#8014](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8014)).

Full Changelog: [v1.40.0...v1.40.1](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/compare/v1.40.0...v1.40.1)

signals.title: Eviction can delete a key mid-full-sync before its baseline is captured, causing the replica to retain keys the master already evicted (#8090, #7925)
signals.text: **Describe the bug** Heartbeat and policy-based eviction delete keys without going through the copy-on-write `OnChange` hook that protects an in-progress full-sync snapshot. This lets eviction delete a key whose bucket a full-sync snapshot hasn't serialized yet (or whose value is mid-flight across multiple serialization chunks), causing the eviction's journal `DEL` to race ahead of — or fall outside — the bucket's still-in-progress baseline stream. The replica then applies the `DEL` as a no-op (the key hasn't finished loading yet) and later inserts the key once its remaining baseline chunks arrive, resurrecting a key the master has already evicted. Result: the replica's keyspace permanently diverges from the master's after an eviction + full-sync race, even though replication offsets report "caught up." There are two separate eviction code paths with this same shape of gap: 1. `DbSlice::FreeMemWithEvictionStepAtomic` (`db_slice.cc:1658`) — heartbeat-driven eviction, called from `EngineShard::RetireExpiredAndEvict` (`engine_shard.cc:931`). 2. `PrimeEvictionPolicy::Evict` (`db_slice.cc:218-256`) — inline policy/maxmemory eviction, fired during dashtable inserts under memory pressure. I opened a partial fix in #8109 (closed) that addresses path 1 only — @vyavdoshenko correctly flagged it as incomplete since path 2 is untouched and is what the second failing test actually exercises. Filing this issue with the full analysis per their suggestion rather than merging that PR. **To Reproduce** Via the existing test suite, intermittently: 1. `tests/dragonfly/replication_specific_test.py::test_heartbeat_eviction_propagation` — populates 233 keys of 1MB each (`DEBUG POPULATE 233 size 1048576`), starts replication, enables heartbeat eviction, waits for eviction to settle, then compares `KEYS *` on master vs. replica. 2. `tests/dragonfly/replication_specific_test.py::test_policy_based_eviction_propagation` — populates data to ~87% of maxmemory with `enable_heartbeat_eviction: false`, starts replication, then runs a seeder to trigger policy-based eviction under memory pressure, then compares keyspaces. Both intermittently fail with a keyspace mismatch (see #8090 and #7925 for CI failure logs). I have not built a standalone reproduction outside this test harness — the race depends on precise timing between eviction and in-flight full-sync serialization, which the tests' large value sizes make more likely to hit but is not deterministic. **Expected behavior** After eviction and a full sync converge (`check_all_replicas_finished` reports caught up), the replica's keyspace should exactly match the master's — no keys the master has already evicted should remain on the replica. **Environment:** - OS: CI runs on `ubuntu-dev:24` (self-hosted ARM64 and GitHub-hosted); locally reproduced/tested on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 - Dragonfly Version: built from `main` at commit `05abfddc5d90733369aaa7f74526870e573653aa` (per #8090's failing CI run) **Additional context** Root cause mechanism, in more detail: both eviction paths delete a key via `DbSlice::Del()` without going through `PreUpdateBlocking`/`CallChangeCallbacks` — the CoW hook that would otherwise force a not-yet-visited bucket's pre-mutation state to be captured before the mutation applies. Both paths skip it because they run under `FiberAtomicGuard`, which disallows the hook's blocking call, so this isn't a simple missed call — it's structurally hard to add without yielding inside an atomic section. Without that protection, eviction can delete a key whose value is currently mid-flight across multiple serialization chunks (large values are split across several `PushToConsumerIfNeeded` calls — see `serializer_base.cc`/`snapshot.cc`). The eviction's journal `DEL` is written as untagged raw bytes into the same output stream and can land between two chunks of that key's own still-in-progress baseline entry. On the replica, `RDB_OPCODE_JOURNAL_BLOB` entries are applied immediately in stream order (`rdb_load.cc:2610-2614`), so the `DEL` becomes a no-op, and once the remaining chunks arrive and the value is fully reassembled, the key gets inserted — resurrecting a key the master no longer has. **Test evidence caveat:** local runs (5x each, 10/10 passing) of `test_heartbeat_eviction_propagation` are solid evidence for path 1, after patching it in #8109. Passing runs of `test_policy_based_eviction_propagation` are **not** meaningful evidence — that fix never touched path 2 (`PrimeEvictionPolicy::Evict`), which is what this test actually exercises (it explicitly disables heartbeat eviction). `snapshot.cc` already has a comment (near `ConsumeJournalChange`) referencing a "delayed deletion queue proposal" in a design doc as the intended comprehensive fix for this class of gap — this may already be on the team's radar architecturally rather than wanting per-call-site patches. **Suggested next steps:** decide whether to extend the `is_snapshot_`/bucket-version guard approach (from #8109) to `PrimeEvictionPolicy::Evict` as well, or pursue the more comprehensive "delayed deletion queue" design instead. Per @vyavdoshenko's feedback on #8109, stronger regression/stress testing under sustained full sync + concurrent memory pressure seems warranted before merging any fix here, given the sensitivity of this code path.

signals.title: fix(server): skip evicting keys in buckets a full sync hasn't capture…
signals.text: Fixes a race between heartbeat/policy-based eviction and full sync that lets a replica retain a key the master has already evicted. **Root cause:** `DbSlice::FreeMemWithEvictionStepAtomic` deletes evicted keys via `Del()` without going through the CoW `OnChange` hook (`PreUpdateBlocking`/`CallChangeCallbacks`) — that hook can't be called here because eviction runs under `FiberAtomicGuard`, which disallows the hook's blocking call. Normally, `OnChange` is what protects an in-progress full-sync snapshot: if a bucket hasn't been serialized yet, it forces the bucket's pre-mutation state to be captured before the mutation is applied. Without that protection, eviction can delete a key whose bucket a full-sync snapshot hasn't visited yet, or whose value is currently mid-flight across multiple chunks (large values get split across several `PushToConsumerIfNeeded` calls). The eviction's journal `DEL` is written as untagged raw bytes into the same output stream and can land *between* two chunks of that key's own still-in-progress baseline entry. On the replica, `RDB_OPCODE_JOURNAL_BLOB` entries are applied immediately in stream order (`rdb_load.cc`), so the `DEL` becomes a no-op (the key hasn't finished loading yet) — and once the remaining chunks arrive and the value is fully reassembled, the key gets inserted, resurrecting a key the master no longer has. `test_heartbeat_eviction_propagation` (#8090) reproduces this directly: it populates 1MB values (`DEBUG POPULATE 233 size 1048576`) against a 300KB serialization chunk size, guaranteeing multi-chunk transmission for the values in play. `test_policy_based_eviction_propagation` (#7925) shows the same failure signature (replica retains a key master evicted) — plausibly the same underlying gap, though I haven't independently confirmed its value sizes hit the identical multi-chunk condition as #8090. ## Fix Before evicting a candidate key, skip it if any currently-registered full-sync consumer either: - hasn't yet serialized that key's bucket (`evict_it.GetVersion() < cb->snapshot_version_`), or - is currently mid-flight serializing some bucket (`cb->IsAnyBucketBlocked()`) Both checks reuse existing non-blocking infrastructure (`DbSlice::change_cb_`, `ChangeConsumerInterface::IsAnyBucketBlocked()`) and add no locking or yielding, so they're safe to call under the existing `FiberAtomicGuard`. Skipped keys remain eligible for eviction on the next heartbeat tick once the snapshot has moved past them — this doesn't reduce total eviction throughput, only defers eviction of specific keys that are momentarily in the race window. ## Test plan - [x] `test_heartbeat_eviction_propagation` — 5/5 passes locally with the fix (previously failing intermittently in CI, see #8090) - [x] `test_policy_based_eviction_propagation` — 5/5 passes locally with the fix (previously failing intermittently in CI, see #7925) - [ ] Not stress-tested: sustained full sync + heavy concurrent memory pressure, to confirm eviction doesn't stall behind a slow-syncing replica for longer than acceptable ## Notes for reviewers This is a targeted mitigation, not the full fix implied by the `snapshot.cc` comment referencing a "delayed deletion queue proposal" design doc — that would presumably address the same class of gap more comprehensively (e.g. for expiry too, not just eviction). Flagging in case this should be superseded by or coordinated with that design work rather than merged as a standalone patch. Fixes #8090 Fixes #7925

signals.title: fix: stop SCRIPT FLUSH from deadlocking against a borrowed interpreter
signals.text: `InterpreterManager::Reset()` blocked until every borrowed interpreter was returned, so `SCRIPT FLUSH` inherited every lock its holders were waiting on. Reset no longer blocks: idle interpreters are destroyed inline, borrowed ones are retired and destroyed by whoever returns them. Three shapes, all reproduced on a debug build: 1. `MULTI; EVAL "return 1" 0; SCRIPT FLUSH; EXEC` - EXEC pre-borrows an interpreter and returns it only after the body ran, so it waits for itself. `SCRIPT` is `NO_KEY_TRANSACTIONAL`, so the EXEC runs as a global transaction: afterwards even `GET` hangs and only `PING` answers. 2. Concurrent `EVAL` + `SCRIPT FLUSH` - the flusher holds `ScriptMgr::mu_` while waiting for an interpreter whose holder is blocked on that same mutex. All scripting wedges permanently. 3. No pre-borrow at all - a keyed `EVAL` holds an interpreter behind the global lock that a concurrent `MULTI; SCRIPT FLUSH; EXEC` holds.

signal.title: Eviction can delete a key mid-full-sync before its baseline is captured, causing the replica to retain keys the master already evicted (#8090, #7925)
signal.text: **Describe the bug** Heartbeat and policy-based eviction delete keys without going through the copy-on-write `OnChange` hook that protects an in-progress full-sync snapshot. This lets eviction delete a key whose bucket a full-sync snapshot hasn't serialized yet (or whose value is mid-flight across multiple serialization chunks), causing the eviction's journal `DEL` to race ahead of — or fall outside — the bucket's still-in-progress baseline stream. The replica then applies the `DEL` as a no-op (the key hasn't finished loading yet) and later inserts the key once its remaining baseline chunks arrive, resurrecting a key the master has already evicted. Result: the replica's keyspace permanently diverges from the master's after an eviction + full-sync race, even though replication offsets report "caught up." There are two separate eviction code paths with this same shape of gap: 1. `DbSlice::FreeMemWithEvictionStepAtomic` (`db_slice.cc:1658`) — heartbeat-driven eviction, called from `EngineShard::RetireExpiredAndEvict` (`engine_shard.cc:931`). 2. `PrimeEvictionPolicy::Evict` (`db_slice.cc:218-256`) — inline policy/maxmemory eviction, fired during dashtable inserts under memory pressure. I opened a partial fix in #8109 (closed) that addresses path 1 only — @vyavdoshenko correctly flagged it as incomplete since path 2 is untouched and is what the second failing test actually exercises. Filing this issue with the full analysis per their suggestion rather than merging that PR. **To Reproduce** Via the existing test suite, intermittently: 1. `tests/dragonfly/replication_specific_test.py::test_heartbeat_eviction_propagation` — populates 233 keys of 1MB each (`DEBUG POPULATE 233 size 1048576`), starts replication, enables heartbeat eviction, waits for eviction to settle, then compares `KEYS *` on master vs. replica. 2. `tests/dragonfly/replication_specific_test.py::test_policy_based_eviction_propagation` — populates data to ~87% of maxmemory with `enable_heartbeat_eviction: false`, starts replication, then runs a seeder to trigger policy-based eviction under memory pressure, then compares keyspaces. Both intermittently fail with a keyspace mismatch (see #8090 and #7925 for CI failure logs). I have not built a standalone reproduction outside this test harness — the race depends on precise timing between eviction and in-flight full-sync serialization, which the tests' large value sizes make more likely to hit but is not deterministic. **Expected behavior** After eviction and a full sync converge (`check_all_replicas_finished` reports caught up), the replica's keyspace should exactly match the master's — no keys the master has already evicted should remain on the replica. **Environment:** - OS: CI runs on `ubuntu-dev:24` (self-hosted ARM64 and GitHub-hosted); locally reproduced/tested on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 - Dragonfly Version: built from `main` at commit `05abfddc5d90733369aaa7f74526870e573653aa` (per #8090's failing CI run) **Additional context** Root cause mechanism, in more detail: both eviction paths delete a key via `DbSlice::Del()` without going through `PreUpdateBlocking`/`CallChangeCallbacks` — the CoW hook that would otherwise force a not-yet-visited bucket's pre-mutation state to be captured before the mutation applies. Both paths skip it because they run under `FiberAtomicGuard`, which disallows the hook's blocking call, so this isn't a simple missed call — it's structurally hard to add without yielding inside an atomic section. Without that protection, eviction can delete a key whose value is currently mid-flight across multiple serialization chunks (large values are split across several `PushToConsumerIfNeeded` calls — see `serializer_base.cc`/`snapshot.cc`). The eviction's journal `DEL` is written as untagged raw bytes into the same output stream and can land between two chunks of that key's own still-in-progress baseline entry. On the replica, `RDB_OPCODE_JOURNAL_BLOB` entries are applied immediately in stream order (`rdb_load.cc:2610-2614`), so the `DEL` becomes a no-op, and once the remaining chunks arrive and the value is fully reassembled, the key gets inserted — resurrecting a key the master no longer has. **Test evidence caveat:** local runs (5x each, 10/10 passing) of `test_heartbeat_eviction_propagation` are solid evidence for path 1, after patching it in #8109. Passing runs of `test_policy_based_eviction_propagation` are **not** meaningful evidence — that fix never touched path 2 (`PrimeEvictionPolicy::Evict`), which is what this test actually exercises (it explicitly disables heartbeat eviction). `snapshot.cc` already has a comment (near `ConsumeJournalChange`) referencing a "delayed deletion queue proposal" in a design doc as the intended comprehensive fix for this class of gap — this may already be on the team's radar architecturally rather than wanting per-call-site patches. **Suggested next steps:** decide whether to extend the `is_snapshot_`/bucket-version guard approach (from #8109) to `PrimeEvictionPolicy::Evict` as well, or pursue the more comprehensive "delayed deletion queue" design instead. Per @vyavdoshenko's feedback on #8109, stronger regression/stress testing under sustained full sync + concurrent memory pressure seems warranted before merging any fix here, given the sensitivity of this code path.

signal.title: fix: stop SCRIPT FLUSH from deadlocking against a borrowed interpreter
signal.text: `InterpreterManager::Reset()` blocked until every borrowed interpreter was returned, so `SCRIPT FLUSH` inherited every lock its holders were waiting on. Reset no longer blocks: idle interpreters are destroyed inline, borrowed ones are retired and destroyed by whoever returns them. Three shapes, all reproduced on a debug build: 1. `MULTI; EVAL "return 1" 0; SCRIPT FLUSH; EXEC` - EXEC pre-borrows an interpreter and returns it only after the body ran, so it waits for itself. `SCRIPT` is `NO_KEY_TRANSACTIONAL`, so the EXEC runs as a global transaction: afterwards even `GET` hangs and only `PING` answers. 2. Concurrent `EVAL` + `SCRIPT FLUSH` - the flusher holds `ScriptMgr::mu_` while waiting for an interpreter whose holder is blocked on that same mutex. All scripting wedges permanently. 3. No pre-borrow at all - a keyed `EVAL` holds an interpreter behind the global lock that a concurrent `MULTI; SCRIPT FLUSH; EXEC` holds.
